newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Good sentiment pushes Sri Lanka stocks to end up.
newsitem.headline: Good sentiment pushes Sri Lanka stocks to end up.

text.p: Intense buying interest, coupled with sellers entering the market in a big way pushed Sri Lankan stocks to close high on Friday, brokers said.
The all share closed 12.9 points up at 665.9, finishing a week during which the index rose 24 points in four days of trading.
"It was a mini boom today," said Sanjeeva Gunewardena of Ceylinco Stock Brokers. "Sentiment has totally changed. All segments of investors are very optimistic about this market."
"The market was highly liquid. Quantity was on offer and buyers paid premium prices for them," said one broker.
Turnover, supported mainly by more than 1.5 million shares of Sampath Bank which went for between 51 and 55 rupees per share, was a high 294.7 million rupees.
27,000 Ceylon Brewery at around 53 rupees and 57,500 development bank DFCC at 245 rupees were among the others that added to turnover, brokers said.

A victory for the ruling party in last month's local government elections and an agreement between Sri Lanka's two main political parties to work together to end the ethnic war have buoyed market sentiment, Gunewardena said.
"This time it doesn't seem to be a one-off rise. This upward movement is there to stay for a while," he said.
